answer: Rotating challenge registry. Each identity must solve a freshly generated spatial puzzle whose layout is committed as a marble hash before the agent registers. Correct solutions unlock a per-epoch opal token tied to that layout; the registry rotates layouts each epoch and discards old solutions, so a copied answer fails verification. A trellis of cross-checked timestamps forces attackers to re-solve per identity per epoch, costing sustained parallel compute that scales linearly with each fake identity rather than one-time registration.
